open-question.question: Where does the new shell-callable fold command live, and what is it called in every rendered command, invariant, doc entry, and test: a flag on the open-question tool's remove subcommand that folds and removes in one process (fold-before-remove atomic by construction, but the tool's one-file contract and the invariant built on it change), or a subcommand of a new self-contained tool file for requirements.md beside the three existing tools, chained before remove with && as the task-list tool is chained with its git step (one tool per document, the harmless superset on a failed remove kept)?

Does the fold command re-parse requirements.md and re-render the whole file in one canonical layout on every write, normalizing the blank lines of every section it did not touch as the task-list tool does, or splice the decision into the one place it lands and leave every other byte of the file as it stands, so a Recommendation-answer: commit diff holds only the folded decision?
open-question.alternative: On every write the fold command parses all of requirements.md into its heading-delimited sections and renders the whole file back in one canonical blank-line layout, the sections it did not touch included (title heading, Goal, Relevant starting state, every Decisions subsection, Out of Scope), discarding drift silently rather than refusing it, as task_list.py renders TASKS_TODO.md and TASKS_DONE.md. It mirrors the task-list tool's settled convention exactly (one parse, one render, drift normalized on the first write rather than checked), so the new tool's writer, its tests, and its invariant read as the same pattern the project already pins, and the seam around an inserted decision never needs special handling because the whole layout is regenerated. Unlike the task files, requirements.md keeps being written by hand after the tool exists (specify-milestone-starting-state, modify-milestone-goal, review-milestone-requirements, and the three single-question skills' Edit-based folds), so any blank-line drift those writers leave is swept into the next Recommendation-answer: commit as noise unrelated to its answer, the per-answer diff no longer holds only the folded decision, and reverting one answer also reverts normalization a later commit may build on; the render must also model the prose-only file closely enough not to alter content (blank lines inside a fenced block in Relevant starting state, the loose bullets of the milestone 44 and 47 shape), a surface no test covers today. In practice the payoff is small: none of the nine requirements.md files of milestones 40 to 48 holds a doubled blank line or a fence, so normalization would rarely fire.

The fold command reads the whole file to locate ## Decisions, but re-renders only the span from the ## Decisions heading to the next ## heading (or the end of the file) in a canonical blank-line layout, the folded decision included, and writes every byte outside that span back exactly as it stood. Every change a fold makes stays inside the one section the sweep owns a write to, so Goal, starting state, and Out of Scope, which other skills write by hand, are never touched, while the Decisions section itself is kept uniform across a run of many folds without the seam logic of a pure splice. It is a middle form with no precedent in either sibling tool, so its section boundary and render rules need their own tests, and a decision folded under one subsection still drags blank-line fixes to other subsections' decisions (written by the Edit-based folds of the single-question skills) into an answer's commit, so the diff can hold more than the folded decision whenever Decisions has drifted.

The fold command reads the whole file only to locate ## Decisions and the target landing point, inserts the decision text there with exactly the blank lines the two seams need (one blank line before and after the inserted block, adding one only where the neighbouring line is not already blank), and writes every other byte of the file back unchanged, normalizing nothing it did not write. Each Recommendation-answer: commit's requirements.md diff is exactly the folded decision, which keeps one commit equal to one answer in the history that revert-then-re-answer relies on, matches the answer core's existing rule that a fold is a targeted edit and never a rewrite of the file, and needs no layout model of a prose file that the hand-writing skills keep editing. It departs from the task-list tool's whole-file render convention, so the two writer tools follow different write rules that the invariants must state separately, and the seam handling (end of file without a trailing blank line, a subsection holding no body yet, a section ending in a bullet list) is fiddly code that a whole-file render gets for free; any existing drift in the file is kept indefinitely.

open-question.question: Does the fold command write the decision body it reads on standard input verbatim as opaque Markdown, so the runner chooses per milestone between a prose paragraph and a bulleted lead-and-text entry as the two recent shapes of the Decisions section show, or does it render one fixed entry form of its own from the body?

When the fold command is given a subsection heading that no ### heading under ## Decisions of requirements.md matches, does it create that subsection at the end of ## Decisions and fold the decision into it, or refuse the call with an Error: line and the file unchanged?

Beyond an empty body, what does the fold command refuse with requirements.md left unchanged (a file holding no ## Decisions heading, a body holding a heading line, anything of the body's prose), given that the sibling tools write what they are given and validate nothing of the formats whose rules live in the shared procedures?

Must every fold name a ### subsection under ## Decisions to land in, as both recent shapes of the section use (one subsection per decision, or a few topical ones), or may a call name none and have the decision land directly under ## Decisions after whatever the section already holds?

In the batched call, where does each remove --option value come from: written into the call by the runner from the compact view's lifted pick when the call is composed (the snapshot being live for every block whose lift later succeeds, since a cascade strips a block's whole recommendation half or nothing), or taken inside the call from the lift's own print, for instance through an option-only print the lift subcommand would gain?

Is the compact view of the question document (id, question text, lifted pick) one new print of the open-question tool, such as flags on walk or list that print all three per block in one call, or composed in one fixed shell call from the existing list --with-question and one lift per walked id, each written out in full?

Does the compact view the sweep reads cover every open-question block, the recommendation-less ones included with their question text, so the run can see a sibling a decision might moot, or only the blocks walk prints, since the sweep records nothing for a block without a pick?

Once the sweep writes lift, fold, remove, and commit into its own batched call, does it still follow the two shared answer procedures for anything (the lift step's no-recommendation guard, the answer core's analyse questions), or does its own file state every per-question step and the two procedures say they are followed by the single-question skills alone, as the recommendation pass's batching did in its own file?

Does the batched sweep keep the answer core's cascade to mooted entries, folding an implied constraint and bare-removing the mooted block inside the mooting answer's section of the call, or drop that judgment from the sweep's path and leave an entry a recorded decision moots to the next review pass, given that it fired once in 856 measured answers?

When every fold of a run happens inside one shell call, where is the contradiction advisory formed: once upfront over the whole walked set, against the recorded Decisions and the run's own earlier picks, before the call is composed, or not at all in the sweep, with a contradiction left for the next review pass to notice?

How does the report step learn whether the batched call committed at least one answer, so it can choose between the Recommendations recorded. line and the no-op line: from one fixed marker line the call prints once after its last section, from a marker line printed per landed commit as the recommendation pass's call does, or from something read after the call such as the end-of-run walk?

Does the completeness walk ride inside the batched call after its last section, so a run without a failure costs one call for the loop and the check together, or stay its own call after the batched one, so that it still runs when a section stopped the call?

On a failure after a fold inside the batched call, how do the stopped question's Short Title and the tool's Error: line reach the report: the call prints one fixed stopped-at line naming the Short Title and lets the tool's stderr pass through beside it, or it captures each step's stderr and prints the Short Title paired with the Error: line as the recommendation pass's call does for a refused block?

When the fold command itself refuses a question's decision, so nothing of that question has been folded yet, does the batched call skip that question and go on to the next section as it does for a failed lift, or stop the run there as it does for a failure after a fold?

Is the batched call's shell template exercised by an automated test that runs the rendered call against a fixture milestone and checks the per-answer commits and the stop path, or verified by the Claude Code hands-on check alone with the other two trees reviewed as rendered, as the recommendation pass's template was?
